title: Running the write sweep
statement: Let $\Gamma$ be a finite alphabet, $N\in\mathbb{N}$, let $E$ inject the symbols of $\Gamma$ together with blank into blocks of $N+1$ optional bits, and let $e:\{0,1\}\hookrightarrow\Gamma$ be an embedding. Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over $\Gamma$, let $x$ be a Boolean input word, let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on the letterwise $e$-image of $x$, and let $a$ be an action over $\Gamma$ with the same number of work tapes as $M$. For every $j\in\mathbb{N}$ with $j\le N$, running the binary block-code simulator for $j+1$ steps from the write-sweep configuration at counter $j$ reaches the move-sweep configuration at counter $N+1$, for the same $c$ and $a$.
